issue.title: sase-1pn landing repairs never landed: slot-refusal policy still lives in Python despite closeout claiming a Rust binding
issue.description:
Epic sase-1pn (task backlog epic 2) landed with a closeout note (2026-10-29T23:08:30Z, author sase-1pn.land) saying its landing tale had moved shared workspace-slot refusal policy behind a Rust binding: "workspace-slot refusal normalization, upsert, conditional clearing, and skip-set policy are in the Rust binding; Python retains Git/filesystem observations, locks, storage, notifications, and rendering." The same note says baseline-aware epic-symbol reconciliation moved into the Rust core binding. Neither change is on master.

Evidence (checked 2026-11-02 against sase origin/master 84e22d98be and sase-core origin/master):
- `git log -- src/sase/workspace_provider/slot_refusal.py` shows a single commit, 01dcc2e5f5 (phase sase-1pn.2). The module is still 448 lines of Python policy: record/clear/stale-clear/list/skip-set/quarantine decisions, with no `sase_core_rs` call.
- sase-core has no slot-refusal code (`git grep -i "slot_refusal|refusal_record|skip_set" origin/master -- '*.rs'` is empty). Its only related commit in the window is 1762b33a (phase .2's allocator skip).
- `src/sase/bead/epic_symbols.py` has no commit between 8bea2e8414 (phase sase-1pn.3) and 5585fadefd (epic sase-1qn's freshness preflight). It contains no baseline-aware local-deletion logic.
- The note's third claim was that a stale contract-manifest row had been removed. On 2026-10-30, sase-1ou.6.land--3 recorded on sase-1pn that the row was still on master. It was later removed by 8f982c8ae9, a different epic's commit.

Likely cause: the landing tale's turn ended with `/sase_plan` proposing task_backlog_epic_3 under the immediate (non-staged) handoff path, and host finalization never committed its edits. Epic 5 lost its landing repairs the same way (sase-1qt notes #6/#8). The epic-2 loss was never detected, so sase-1p9 and sase-1pn are closed with a claim the code does not support.

Scope: move the slot-refusal decision policy (record validation and normalization, upsert, conditional clearing, skip-set computation) behind a sase-core wire/binding. Keep Python host I/O, locking, notifications, and rendering, per the Rust core backend boundary. Separately confirm whether the "upstream row union blocks same-turn local cleanup" close refusal the sase-1pn lander reproduced is still live after 5585fadefd. It is the same mechanism that held phase sase-1pu.5.1.4 unclosable from 2026-10-30 09:01Z to 2026-11-01 14:51Z. If it is still live, fix it here or route it to its owner.

task_type_fields.impact: Shared workspace-allocation policy is implemented only in Python, so any other frontend must re-implement it. The bead history records a fix that never shipped, which misleads anyone auditing the workspace provider.
task_type_fields.repro: 1) git log --format='%h %s' -- src/sase/workspace_provider/slot_refusal.py  -> only 01dcc2e5f5. 2) grep -n sase_core_rs src/sase/workspace_provider/slot_refusal.py -> no match. 3) In linked sase-core: git grep -i 'slot_refusal' origin/master -- '*.rs' -> no match. 4) Compare with sase-1pn closeout note at 2026-10-29T23:08:30Z claiming the Rust move.

issue.creation_reason: Epic 2's landing closeout claims Rust-boundary repairs that never landed. The Python slot-refusal policy still violates the required Rust core boundary, and no open bead tracks it because sase-1p9 and sase-1pn were closed on the unlanded claim.

payload.description: Closed on the sase-1pn closeout's unlanded claim that quarantine policy moved to Rust
